text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG, soon to be merged with Norddeutsche Landesbank to form one of Germany's biggest financial institutions, on Friday reported a steep rise in operating profit in the first six months of 1997.
Operating profit after risk provisions more than doubled to 635 million marks, driven by a surge in income from the bank's growing real estate services business.

Earnings were also boosted by a 13 percent rise in net commission income to 383 million marks and a swing in own-account trading income to a profit of 153 million marks from a year-earlier loss of 110 million marks.
The results mark a turnaround from a weak 1996 when Bankgesellschaft set aside 2.5 billion marks to cover loan risks caused by an economic slump in its core region of Berlin and east Germany.

"Based on the year to date we can be confident of returning to a satisfactory result in 1997," it said in its interim report. Last year net profit dwindled by 90 percent to 47 million marks as the bank cleared up its loan portfolio.
Risk provisions would fall sharply to 500 million marks this year, the bank said.
The rise in first-half operating profit was stonger than expected and Bankgesellschaft's shares rose 1.60 marks or 3.4 percent to 48.75 marks on a day of steep losses in the overall market.
Several analysts maintained their hold recommendations for the stock after the results.
They noted that net interest income fell 5.0 percent to 1.82 billion marks -- a sign of increased caution in lending after the bank got stung last year.

"The interest income was disappointing, the fall resulted from strong pressure on the interest margin as the bank streamlined its loan portfolio," said Nathalie Grasegger, banking analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank.
The caution was reflected in a stagnation in group lending, which rose just 1.8 percent to 235 billion marks in the first six months.

Bankgesellschaft said its income from other activities jumped 57.4 percent to 524 million marks and largely resulted from the bank's growing real estate services business, which includes services such as construction project management.
The expansion in that field also drove up administration costs which rose 12.5 percent to 1.99 billion marks.
Bankgesellschaft, 56.8 percent-owned by the state of Berlin, is working out plans to merge with Norddeutsche Landesbank (NordLB), a state-owned regional bank, by mid-1998.
Based on first-half data the two banks have a combined balance sheet total of 592 billion marks, just below Dresdner Bank AG, Germany's second largest commercial bank.

The overcrowded banking sector is undergoing a consolidation drive which most recently saw the announcement of a planned merger by two Bavarian banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, which will form a bank bigger even than Dresdner.
